The mean is (1.0+0.9+0.8+0.9+0.8+1.0+0.8+0.7+0.9)/9 = 0.87. Adjustment components: level effect +0.00 because the 12-month private compensation pace was 3.4 percent in Q1; momentum effect +0.02 because Q1 rebounded from 0.7 to 0.9; labor-demand effect -0.03 because June payrolls were +57,000 with 4.2 percent unemployment; benefits and health-cost persistence +0.04 because Q1 private benefits were +1.3. Point = 0.87+0.00+0.02-0.03+0.04 = 0.90. Interval method uses the sample standard deviation of the nine matching qoq values themselves: sigma = 0.10 percentage point, so 1.28*sigma = 0.128; I use a 0.15-point half-width, within 1.75x, to allow one-decimal publication rounding and benefit-cost lumpiness, giving 0.75 to 1.05 on the latent percent-growth scale."},{"kind":"text","text":"Counter-considerations: upside risk is another benefits-heavy print or renewed professional-services wage pressure that would land above the interval, especially a rounded 1.1 percent first print.
